commits.headline: perf(tools): overlay_asm disassembles the levels in parallel
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Each level is its own spimdisasm call writing its own folders, so
_run_jobs runs them in a process pool, one per level up to the cores
there are. The output is the same: tools/setup_asm.sh wrote all 3,431
overlay files with it, and the build after it is exact (1220/1220,
the whole image matches retail). Under the container's emulation the
two passes went from about an hour to minutes.

commits.headline: fix(tools): ps2eeas_nops measures the second assembly too; match func_L00_002AE278
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body: GNU as can pad a short loop in the second assembly that it left alone in the first (the nops added elsewhere move its fragment boundaries). The build and try_func now run ps2eeas_nops once more on the second assembly and reassemble if anything changed. The tool reads its own output back: .word branches count as branches and an mfc1 in its own noreorder block as a rule-4 site, so a finished object stays unchanged (all game objects checked). This unblocks func_L00_002AE278, whose match padded a…
